_note: Axis-A color conformance under a PERCEPTUAL color-loss metric: the analyzer decodes the OUTPUT by its own embedded tag and the SOURCE forced to its matrix/range (fixtures carry only a matrix tag), then asks 'does the export SHOW the same colors as the source?'. ALL FOUR encodings are FAITHFUL (worst_app_max <= faithfulMax). 709ltd/601ltd decode the ORIGINAL (DirectExport); 709full/601full decode a PROXY (yuvj420p is off the DirectExport whitelist) made self-describing by the recipe (source_color_args + write_colr, proxy v7/quick-q4) and additionally covered by threading the ffprobe sourceColor into proxy decodes -- mediabunny reads only the mp4 colr atom (never the SPS VUI) and the WebView2 decoder follows the config over the VUI, so a colr-less proxy decode used to fall back to bt709/limited and misread full-range (pc-as-tv clip+stretch) and 601 (601-as-709) proxies. The decoder's frame then converts through VideoClipSprite's colorSpace-honoring 2D drawImage (Pixi's copyExternalImageToTexture ignores VideoFrame.colorSpace). The WebCodecs HD encoder ignores the input frame colorSpace and writes a resolution default, so every HD output is bt709/limited-tagged: 601 sources are faithfully NORMALIZED to 709 and full-range sources faithfully CONVERTED to limited, costing only codec round-trip. ADR 0014.
